rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), as described in CRD Housing FAQ (calcivilrights.ca.gov/housing)
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers covered by FEHA, including landlords, property managers and tenant screening companies, for most housing accommodations in California.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied home renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics (per the FAQ), but may not publish discriminatory statements or advertisements.
rules.quoted_span: Refusing to rent to a tenant with a section 8 voucher.
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent to an applicant because of their source of income, including a Section 8 voucher. They must also comply with the paperwork and inspection requirements of rental assistance programs.
rules.title: Source of income discrimination barred, including Section 8 vouchers

rules.citation: LAHD, RSO Rent Increase Calculator (housing.lacity.gov/rso-rent-increase-calculator); City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).
rules.interaction: Applies on top of the annual allowable RSO increase, which previously could include an additional utility percentage.
rules.key_value: 0% additional utility increase
rules.quoted_span: Beginning February 2, 2026, a landlord can no longer include any additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.requirement: Beginning February 2, 2026, landlords of RSO units can no longer add any extra percentage increase for utilities on top of the annual allowable rent increase.
rules.title: No additional utility percentage added to RSO rent increase

rules.coverage_conditions: Any person or agent who threatens or takes reprisals against a tenant of residential premises.
rules.exemptions: The presumption does not apply to a notice of termination for nonpayment of rent.
rules.interaction: Any waiver of this provision in a lease or other rental agreement is void and unenforceable.
rules.key_value: Damages of 1 to 3 months' rent, or actual damages if greater, plus costs and attorney's fees; 6-month rebuttable presumption
rules.quoted_span: shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities.
rules.requirement: A landlord may not threaten or take reprisals, including terminating the tenancy, against a tenant who reports code violations, enforces housing laws, or organizes or joins a tenants' union. A termination notice, rent increase, or substantial change in tenancy terms within six months of such activity is presumed to be a reprisal, and the landlord can rebut that only by clear and convincing evidence.
rules.title: Anti-reprisal protection against retaliatory termination of tenancy

rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, DND (Feb. 2017), Credit ¶ 5(a)
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.interaction: Credit history may still be considered only as described in the credit history provision of this policy.
rules.key_value: No credit score use
rules.quoted_span: The agent agrees not to use the applicant credit score to approve or deny housing applications.
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers may not use an applicant's credit score to approve or deny a housing application.
rules.title: Fair Chance: no use of credit score to approve or deny applications

rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (adopted 2021)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies covered by the Just Cause Eviction Ordinance that are terminated for no-fault reasons such as owner occupancy, withdrawal from the rental market, or demolition or substantial remodel.
rules.exemptions: Properties excluded from the Just Cause Eviction Ordinance.
rules.key_value: 3 months relocation assistance or 3 months rent waived
rules.quoted_span: Under a no-fault just cause termination, the owner shall either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive payment of rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy.
rules.requirement: When ending a tenancy for a no-fault just cause, the owner must either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy.
rules.title: Relocation assistance for no-fault terminations

rules.citation: California Assembly Bill 12 (as described by Berkeley Rent Board)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies under California law. The two-month limit applies only to landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total, where ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or LLC whose members are all natural persons.
rules.interaction: Replaces the pre-July 1, 2024 limits of two months' rent for unfurnished units and three months' rent for furnished units. The Berkeley Rent Board cannot determine whether a landlord may charge one or two months' rent for a new tenancy.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords)
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units
rules.requirement: Landlords may generally charge no more than one month's rent as a security deposit, for both furnished and unfurnished units. Small landlords may charge up to two months' rent. Last month's rent counts toward the deposit, but first month's rent does not.
rules.title: Security deposit cap (AB 12)

rules.coverage_conditions: Rental dwelling units offered by a housing provider.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded.
rules.key_value: Barred: non-conviction arrests/charges, expunged, pardoned, vacated, sealed records, juvenile adjudications
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not, either before or after the issuance of a conditional offer, evaluate an applicant based on any of the following types of criminal records:
rules.requirement: Before or after a conditional offer, a landlord may not evaluate an applicant based on arrests or charges without conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated or sealed records, or juvenile adjudications.
rules.title: Categories of criminal records that may never be considered

rules.citation: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482); Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12
rules.coverage_conditions: Buildings older than 15 years, applied on a rolling basis. A unit built January 1, 2006 is covered on and after January 1, 2021.
rules.exemptions: Units constructed within the last 15 years. Units deed- or regulatory-restricted for low- or moderate-income households. Certain dormitories. A two-unit property where the owner occupied the second unit for the entire tenancy. Single-family homes and condominiums are exempt from the state law if not owned by a real estate trust, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, and the tenant received the required written notice (Civ. Code 1946.2(e)(8)(B)(i) and 1947.12(d)(5)(B)(i)). That exemption does not apply where there is more than one dwelling unit on the lot, or a second unit that cannot be sold separately. Units subject to the City's RSO are also not covered.
rules.interaction: The Los Angeles JCO does not itself regulate rent increases. The state cap applies to units outside the RSO. The page lists 8.9% as the maximum for Aug 1, 2024 to Jul 31, 2025, so the current-year percentage is not stated.
rules.key_value: Lesser of 5% + regional cost-of-living change, or 10%
rules.quoted_span: rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower
rules.requirement: For covered buildings, annual rent increases are capped at 5% plus the regional change in cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower. The page does not regulate rent increases under the JCO and points to this state law.
rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act (AB 1482) annual rent cap, as described by LAHD

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any 'person' (as defined in Bus. & Prof. Code § 16702), excluding the end consumer. 'Common pricing algorithm' means any methodology, including software, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or otherwise influence a price or commercial term. Commercial terms include level of service, availability, and output.
rules.exemptions: End consumers of a product or service are not 'persons' under the section.
rules.interaction: Does not impair or limit the applicability of other antitrust laws (subsection (c)).
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if you coerce another person to set or adopt the price or commercial term the algorithm recommends. This is a general pricing rule and is not limited to housing, but it reaches rent-setting software.
rules.title: Unlawful coercion to adopt common pricing algorithm recommendations

rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords or agents who fail to comply with subsection 6 clauses (a), (d) or (e).
rules.interaction: Works together with the forfeiture provisions of subsection 6.
rules.key_value: 3x deposit plus 5% interest, costs and attorney's fees
rules.quoted_span: If the lessor or his agent fails to comply with clauses (a), (d), or (e) of subsection 6, the tenant shall be awarded damages in an amount equal to three times the amount of such security deposit or balance thereof to which the tenant is entitled plus interest at the rate of five per cent from the date when such payment became due, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.requirement: If a landlord fails to hold the deposit properly, fails to return it as required, or violates the related provisions listed in subsection 6(a), (d) or (e), the tenant is awarded three times the deposit owed plus 5% interest, court costs and attorney's fees.
rules.title: Treble damages for deposit violations

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords (as defined in SDMC § 98.0702) of residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Excludes software that publishes reports from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old or from public information and does not recommend rates for future leases or renewals; also excludes software used to set rents or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.interaction: Remedies are cumulative with other remedies at law, statute, or ordinance. Takes effect on the thirtieth day after final passage; the document is an unadopted draft with blank passage date.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.requirement: A landlord may not use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property. Each month the violation continues, and each property where it is used, is a separate violation; tenants may sue for injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation plus attorney's fees.
rules.title: Prohibition on landlord use of algorithmic devices to set rents or occupancy

rules.coverage_conditions: Any lessor of residential real property, or agent, who accepts a security deposit.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.interaction: A deposit above one month's rent is only allowed if the tenant is given the statement of condition (subsec. 1(b)(iii)). Damage listed in the statement cannot be deducted from the deposit.
rules.key_value: Statement of condition within 10 days of tenancy start or deposit receipt, whichever is later
rules.quoted_span: Any lessor of residential real property, or his agent, who accepts a security deposit from a tenant or prospective tenant shall, upon receipt of such security deposit, or within ten days after commencement of the tenancy, whichever is later, furnish to such tenant or prospective tenant a separate written statement of the present condition of the premises to be leased or rented.
rules.requirement: When taking a security deposit, a landlord must give a signed receipt and, within ten days of the tenancy starting or receipt of the deposit (whichever is later), a separate written statement of the premises' condition listing existing damage. The tenant has 15 days to return it with corrections.
rules.title: Move-in statement of condition and deposit receipt

rules.coverage_conditions: Newly constructed rental units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979; tenancies eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act; and some tenancies where the rent is regulated by another government agency.
rules.interaction: Units exempt from the Ordinance's rent increase limitations remain subject to its eviction provisions.
rules.quoted_span: Some tenancies that are exempt from the rent increase limitations of the Ordinance are still subject to the eviction provisions of the Ordinance, and tenants in these categories can only be evicted for one of the “just cause” reasons listed in the Ordinance.
rules.requirement: Tenancies exempt from the Rent Ordinance's rent increase limits, such as newer construction, can still only be ended for one of the listed just cause reasons.
rules.title: Just cause protections extend to units exempt from rent increase limits

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (as amended by Measure BB, Nov. 2024)
rules.coverage_conditions: Owner move-in evictions from units covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.key_value: Annual inflationary adjustment
rules.quoted_span: The Rent Board must make inflationary adjustments to owner move-in eviction relocation assistance amounts each year.
rules.requirement: The Rent Board must adjust owner move-in eviction relocation assistance amounts for inflation every year.
rules.title: Annual inflation adjustment of owner move-in relocation assistance

rules.citation: 15 U.S.C. § 1681m; Truth in Renting guide, Credit Checks and Background Checks
rules.coverage_conditions: Prospective residential tenants.
rules.key_value: Reasonable fee (no numeric cap stated)
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may also request reasonable rental application fees or employment verification.
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge the cost of a credit report and may request reasonable rental application fees. The guide states no specific dollar cap.
rules.title: Rental application fees must be reasonable

rules.coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling. Does not apply to security collected or demanded before 2024-07-01.
rules.exemptions: Advance payment of not less than six months' rent when the lease term is six months or longer; mutually agreed paid alterations requested by the tenant; small-landlord two-month cap under (c)(5).
rules.interaction: Yields to the two-month cap for qualifying small landlords in (c)(5) and to the service member provisions in (c)(4) and (c)(5)(B).
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent
rules.quoted_span: Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive a security deposit (however named) greater than one month's rent, in addition to the first month's rent paid before move-in. A prepayment of six or more months' rent is allowed for leases of six months or longer.
rules.title: Security deposit cap of one month's rent

rules.citation: Los Angeles Municipal Code ch. XV, art. 1 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance)
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28. Covered types include apartments, duplexes, ADUs/JADUs, and mobile homes in parks. Condominiums and townhomes are not rent-regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995.
rules.exemptions: Rent may go to market rate if the tenant voluntarily moves out, is evicted for non-payment or a lease violation, is evicted for failing to comply with a Tenant Habitability Plan, is evicted per a City Attorney order, or accepts a Tenant Buyout Agreement. A Luxury Exemption is available on application.
rules.interaction: Additional increases beyond the allowable percentage (capital improvement, primary renovation, seismic retrofit, rehabilitation, just and reasonable) require LAHD approval.
rules.key_value: Once per 12 months, by the annual allowable rent increase percentage
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage
rules.requirement: Landlords of rent-stabilized units may raise rent only once every 12 months, and only by the allowable percentage set by the city. Rent may be raised to market rate only in the circumstances the page lists, such as the tenant voluntarily moving out or being evicted for non-payment or a lease violation.
rules.title: RSO annual allowable rent increase

rules.coverage_conditions: Service member (Military and Veterans Code § 400) renting residential property in which the service member will reside; applies on or after 2025-04-01.
rules.interaction: Applies where security is charged above the standard amount pursuant to the (c)(1) cap.
rules.key_value: Return of additional security after no more than 6 months of residency
rules.quoted_span: On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security pursuant to paragraph (1) due to the credit history, credit score, housing history, or other factor related to the tenant, the landlord shall provide the tenant with a written statement, on or before the date the lease is signed, of the amount of the higher security and an explanation why the higher security amount is being charged.
rules.requirement: If a landlord charges a service member a higher than standard or advertised security because of credit history, credit score, housing history or similar factors, the landlord must give a written statement of the higher amount and the reason on or before lease signing. The additional amount must be returned after no more than six months if the tenant is not in arrears.
rules.title: Higher security charged to service members: written explanation and return

rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies statewide. Local rent control or rent leveling ordinances apply where municipalities have adopted them.
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control for 30 years after completion; government-subsidized rents may also be exempt.
rules.interaction: Municipal rent control ordinances govern the amount of any increase; the state standard is unconscionability.
rules.key_value: No unconscionable increase; local rent control ordinances apply
rules.quoted_span: The increase in rent must not be unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
rules.requirement: New Jersey has no statewide rent control. A landlord may raise rent only at lease termination with proper written notice. The increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with any municipal rent control ordinance.
rules.title: Rent increases must not be unconscionable

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (as amended by Measure BB, Nov. 2024)
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully or partially covered units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.key_value: 3 business days
rules.quoted_span: The landlord must file with the Rent Board a copy of any notice to terminate a tenancy, notice to quit, and summons and complaint no later than three business days after the tenant was served with the document.
rules.requirement: Termination notices must state that advice is available from the Rent Board and give its counseling phone number and website. Landlords must file copies of termination notices, notices to quit and summons and complaints with the Rent Board within three business days of serving the tenant.
rules.title: Eviction notices must include Rent Board information and be filed with Rent Board

rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, DND (Feb. 2017), Credit ¶ 5(b)-(c)
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.interaction: Mitigating circumstances (representative payer or third-party guarantor, disability-related insufficient credit, other circumstances) must be considered where insufficient credit is the basis for rejection.
rules.key_value: Credit history only in lieu of unavailable rental history
rules.quoted_span: Property Managers may consider an applicant’s credit history, but such information may ONLY be used in lieu of rental history to determine an applicant’s ability to pay rent when rental history is not available.
rules.requirement: Credit history may be used only to judge ability to pay rent when rental history is not available. Lack of credit history, as opposed to poor credit history, is not sufficient justification to reject an applicant, and ability to pay must be shown through an identifiable source of sufficient income and prior rental history.
rules.title: Fair Chance: credit history only in lieu of rental history

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance (Rent Board Guide to Coverage)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to fully covered units (most multifamily built before 1980; single-family homes with tenancies beginning before 1996; rooming houses) and partially covered units (new construction with Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980; single-family tenancies beginning on or after January 1, 1996; most condominiums; certain HUD-subsidized units).
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplex; units where the owner shares a kitchen or bath with the tenant; tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018 on properties with an ADU where either unit is owner-occupied; university rental units; nonprofit cooperatives.
rules.interaction: Unlike rent control and just cause, security deposit interest also applies to partially covered units. The guide does not state the interest rate.
rules.quoted_span: Most condominiums** Partially Covered Yes No Yes Yes
rules.requirement: Security deposit interest requirements apply to fully covered and partially covered units, including new construction after June 1980, post-1996 single-family tenancies, and most condominiums. Exempt units are not subject to the requirement.
rules.title: Berkeley security deposit interest coverage

rules.coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.exemptions: Documentation requirements need not be met if deductions for repairs and cleaning do not exceed $125 or the tenant validly waived them; a landlord may use good-faith estimates when work or documents cannot be completed within 21 days.
rules.interaction: A landlord who fails in bad faith to comply may not claim any amount of the security (h)(7); statutory damages up to twice the deposit under subdivision (m).
rules.key_value: 21 calendar days
rules.quoted_span: the landlord shall furnish the tenant, a copy of an itemized statement indicating the basis for, and the amount of, any security received and the disposition of the security, and shall return any remaining portion of the security to the tenant as follows:
rules.requirement: Within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must give the tenant an itemized statement of the basis for and amount of any deductions and return any remaining deposit. Documentation of repair and cleaning charges must accompany the statement, with exceptions for deductions of $125 or less or a valid waiver.
rules.title: Return of deposit and itemized statement within 21 days

rules.coverage_conditions: Rental of housing; applies to persons residing or proposing to reside together.
rules.quoted_span: To use a financial or income standard in the rental of housing that fails to account for the aggregate income of persons residing together or proposing to reside together on the same basis as the aggregate income
rules.requirement: A landlord's financial or income standard must account for the combined income of people who live or plan to live together on the same basis as it does for married persons.
rules.title: Aggregate income of co-residents must be counted like married couples

rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance.
rules.interaction: Applies even to some tenancies exempt from the Ordinance's rent increase limits, including units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for a rent increase under Costa-Hawkins, and some tenancies regulated by another government agency.
rules.key_value: 17 enumerated just cause reasons under Ordinance Section 37.9(a)
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of the enumerated just cause reasons, and that reason must be the dominant motive for the eviction. Expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership is not just cause.
rules.title: Just cause required to evict from Rent Ordinance-covered units

rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies. Move-in photographs required for tenancies beginning on or after 2025-07-01; move-out and post-repair photographs required beginning 2025-04-01.
rules.interaction: Photographs under subdivision (g) must be provided with the itemized statement under (h)(2)(D) when deductions are made.
rules.quoted_span: Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord, but prior to any repairs or cleanings for which the landlord will make a deduction from or claim against the security deposit pursuant to this section, and shall also take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after such repairs or cleanings are completed.
rules.requirement: Landlords must photograph the unit at the start of tenancies beginning on or after 2025-07-01. Beginning 2025-04-01, they must also photograph the unit after possession is returned and again after repairs or cleanings, and provide the photographs when deducting for them.
rules.title: Photographs required before and after repairs; at tenancy inception

rules.citation: LAHD, RSO Rent Increase Calculator (housing.lacity.gov/rso-rent-increase-calculator); City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO). The page does not state year-built or certificate-of-occupancy cutoffs; it refers users to ZIMAS to check whether a unit is covered.
rules.exemptions: Non-RSO properties are not covered by this figure. The page only refers users to the Housing Department for their allowable increases.
rules.interaction: The stated 3% figure applies only to the period ending 2026-06-30, which is before the 2026-10-01 query date. The ordinance continues, but the figure for the later period is not given in this document. State law separately requires 30 days' written notice for increases under 10%.
rules.key_value: 3% annual allowable increase (July 1, 2025 - June 30, 2026)
rules.quoted_span: Annual rent increases for rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), effective
rules.requirement: For units covered by the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, the page states the annual allowable rent increase is 3% for the period July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026. The page does not state the figure for any later period.
rules.title: RSO annual allowable rent increase (3%)

rules.citation: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance, Cambridge Municipal Code ch. 14.04
rules.coverage_conditions: Real estate transactions covered by the Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance, including viewing or renting an apartment and terms and conditions of tenancy.
rules.exemptions: Exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
rules.quoted_span: Source of Income, includes Section 8 and public benefits
rules.requirement: Landlords and rental agents may not discriminate in renting an apartment or in the terms of a tenancy based on a person's source of income, including Section 8 and public benefits. Tenant selection standards must be reasonable and applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.
rules.title: Source of income is a protected category under Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenancies where just cause is required under subdivision (a) and the termination is for a no-fault just cause (owner move-in, withdrawal from rental market, government or court order to vacate, demolition or substantial remodel).
rules.exemptions: No relocation assistance if a government agency or court determines the tenant is at fault for the condition that triggered a vacate order.
rules.interaction: Relocation assistance or rent waiver is credited against any other relocation assistance required by other law.
rules.key_value: One month of the tenant's rent in effect when the notice was issued; payment within 15 calendar days of service of the notice
rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation assistance or rent waiver shall be equal to one month of the tenant’s rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminate the tenancy.
rules.requirement: If an owner terminates a covered tenancy for a no-fault just cause, the owner must either pay the tenant relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent, regardless of the tenant's income. The termination notice must tell the tenant of this right, and failure to strictly comply makes the notice void.
rules.title: Relocation assistance or rent waiver for no-fault terminations

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any rental property owner (a person owning one or more rental residential dwelling units, directly or indirectly) and their agents, representatives or subcontractors. Residential dwelling units exclude inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities.
rules.exemptions: Coordinating function excludes research/statistical/testing use not used to set or recommend rents or lease terms, free public rent estimates, equal-terms real estate brokerage databases that do not set or recommend prices, and government affordability controls.
rules.interaction: Additional to the New Jersey Antitrust Act, whose enforcement provisions (C.56:9-6 through 9-17) still apply; municipalities may not enact conflicting ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator;
rules.requirement: Landlords, and their agents or subcontractors, may not subscribe to, contract for, or pay for the services of a coordinator, meaning a provider of algorithmic pricing software or devices that performs a coordinating function. Violations are violations of the New Jersey Antitrust Act.
rules.title: Landlords barred from paying for coordinator (algorithmic pricing) services

rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, DND (Feb. 2017), § 1
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy; also applied to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and/or an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the safety of others, or to current criminal behavior.
rules.interaction: Federal or state law imposing a conflicting criminal history requirement preempts this policy.
rules.key_value: No consideration of non-conviction arrests, judicially relieved convictions, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old
rules.quoted_span: The Developer/Agent (Agent) agrees to not consider any of the following categories when determining housing eligibility and or considering eviction:
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers may not use a blanket policy denying housing based on arrests or convictions and must review applicants case by case. They may not consider non-conviction arrests, convictions subject to judicial relief, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old when deciding eligibility or considering eviction.
rules.title: Fair Chance: limits on use of criminal records in tenant selection

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board Regulation 1148; Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.76.110A
rules.coverage_conditions: Eligible landlords under Rent Board Regulation 1148; the 2026 AGA may not adjust rents of tenants whose tenancy began on or after January 1, 2025 and whose rents were set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.
rules.exemptions: Tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 with rents set under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act are not adjusted by the 2026 AGA.
rules.interaction: Annual formula under Berkeley Municipal Code section 13.76.110A (65% of CPI, approved by voters in November 2004). Qualifying conditions and tenant notice requirements are set out in Regulation 1148.
rules.key_value: 1.0% for 2026 (65% of CPI increase of 1.5%)
rules.quoted_span: The 2026 AGA of 1.0% represents 65% of the increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for All Urban Consumers in the Bay Area during the period from July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025, which was 1.5% as posted by the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
rules.requirement: Eligible landlords may raise the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026. The 1.0% equals 65% of the 1.5% Bay Area CPI increase for July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025.
rules.title: Berkeley 2026 Annual General Adjustment (AGA) of 1.0%

rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (section number not stated in document)
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you.
rules.requirement: A landlord must have a valid reason to evict a tenant, such as nonpayment of rent, breach of the lease, or the landlord moving into the unit. Landlords may have to help pay relocation costs for certain no-fault evictions.
rules.title: Just cause required for eviction

rules.coverage_conditions: Prospective tenants applying for residential rental units in Berkeley; landlords charging a fee for a consumer credit report and application processing.
rules.interaction: Fee cap derives from California Civil Code Section 1950.6; the city page restates the state law limit.
rules.key_value: $68.96 maximum screening fee for 2026
rules.quoted_span: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a tenant screening fee only up to the annual maximum, which is $68.96 for 2026. Landlords must provide a receipt, an itemized list of expenses, a copy of the credit report, and refund any unused portion of the fee.
rules.title: Maximum tenant screening fee and related applicant protections

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all cities and towns. The exception applies only to a city or town that accepts chapter 40P. Even then, regulation cannot apply to any rental unit owned by a person or entity owning fewer than ten rental units, or to any unit with a fair market rent exceeding $400.
rules.exemptions: Any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that meets the conditions in (a)-(c). Compliance becomes voluntary for owners after six months from initial adoption. The regulation may not cover occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion or removal of properties from regulation.
rules.interaction: Preempts local rent control ordinances. The permitted local regulation is limited to the voluntary, compensated form in (a)-(c) and cannot regulate evictions.
rules.key_value: Rent control prohibited; narrow voluntary exception (owners of fewer than 10 units or units with fair market rent over $400 are not covered)
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind
rules.requirement: No Massachusetts city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind. A municipality that accepts chapter 40P may adopt only voluntary rent control regulation, and must compensate owners of controlled units from general funds.
rules.title: Statewide prohibition on local rent control

rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies terminated for no-fault just cause under § 98.0704(b) in residential rental property subject to the Division.
rules.exemptions: No relocation assistance for habitability or vacate orders where a government agency or court finds the tenant at fault.
rules.interaction: Credited against any other relocation assistance required by federal, state or other local law. It is in addition to return of the security deposit.
rules.key_value: 2 months' rent (3 months if tenant is a senior aged 62+ or disabled)
rules.quoted_span: Unless section 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii) applies, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice.
rules.requirement: For no-fault terminations, the landlord must give the tenant relocation assistance, either as a direct payment or a rent waiver, regardless of the tenant's income or length of tenancy. The amount is two months of actual rent, or three months if the tenant is a senior or disabled.
rules.title: Relocation assistance for no-fault terminations

rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property where the tenancy lasts more than 30 days (fixed terms of three months or less are not a tenancy). Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years is exempt, unless it is a mobilehome.
rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotels; short-term residential occupancy; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (Section 8 is not exempt); mobilehomes under the Mobilehome Residency Law; nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, care facilities and non-profit transitional housing; dormitories; units sharing a bathroom or kitchen with a resident landlord; owner-occupied single-family residences renting up to two bedrooms or two ADUs/JADUs; duplexes where the landlord occupies one unit; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); and separately alienable property whose landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member or mobilehome park management and which gave the required written exemption notice.
rules.interaction: Consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2. Rights are in addition to state or federal tenant rights.
rules.key_value: Just cause (at-fault or no-fault) required
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause.
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy unless there is just cause, which is either at-fault or no-fault cause as defined in the Division. Failure to comply with the Division's notice requirements voids the termination notice.
rules.title: Just cause required to terminate a tenancy

rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property, including units in mobilehome parks, where the tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied for 12 months. Does not cover a homeowner of a mobilehome. The section became operative April 1, 2024 and is repealed as of January 1, 2030.
rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotels; nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care and licensed residential care facilities; dormitories owned and operated by higher education institutions or K-12 schools; units where the tenant shares a bathroom or kitchen with an owner-occupant; single-family owner-occupied residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms; a duplex where the owner occupies one unit; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); separately alienable property whose owner is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member and which has the required written exemption notice; and deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or adopted or amended after that date and found more protective. A property cannot be subject to both a local ordinance and this section.
rules.key_value: 12 months of continuous lawful occupancy (24 months if adult tenants added)
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months, the owner may only end the tenancy for a statutory at-fault or no-fault just cause, and the cause must be stated in the written termination notice. If additional adult tenants were added before an existing tenant reached 24 months, protection applies only once all tenants have 12 months or one tenant has 24 months.
rules.title: Just cause required to terminate a tenancy after 12 months

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property (any dwelling or unit intended for human habitation, including units in a mobilehome park), except exempt property. Housing is exempt if it was issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless it is a mobilehome. For mobilehome tenancies it applies only to rent increases occurring on or after 2021-02-18. It does not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; dormitories of higher education or K-12 schools; housing under a stricter local rent control; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable property whose owner is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management and which has the required written notice; a duplex where the owner occupies one unit as a principal residence (and neither unit is an ADU or JADU).
rules.interaction: Subdivision (b) lets the owner set the initial rent for a new tenancy in which no prior tenant remains in lawful possession; the cap applies only to later increases. Housing under a local rent control that restricts annual increases to less than this cap is exempt. The section does not authorize local governments to set limits beyond what Chapter 2.7 (Civ. Code § 1954.50 et seq.) allows.
rules.key_value: lesser of (5% + local CPI change) or 10% per 12 months
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
rules.requirement: A landlord may not raise the gross rent for a unit by more than 5 percent plus the local percentage change in cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period. The cap is measured against the lowest gross rent charged during the 12 months before the increase takes effect, excluding discounts, incentives, concessions and credits that the tenant accepted.
rules.title: Statewide annual rent increase cap

rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property subject to the Division (see exemptions in § 98.0703).
rules.exemptions: Properties exempt under § 98.0703.
rules.interaction: Many grounds cross-reference California Code of Civil Procedure section 1161. The landlord must notify the San Diego Housing Commission within three business days of the tenant notice once the Commission's submission portal is operating.
rules.key_value: 12 enumerated at-fault grounds
rules.quoted_span: At-fault just cause is any of the following:
rules.requirement: A landlord may terminate a tenancy for at-fault cause only on the listed grounds, such as nonpayment of rent, material lease breach, nuisance, waste, criminal activity or refusal to sign a similar lease renewal. For curable lease violations the landlord must first give written notice and an opportunity to cure.
rules.title: At-fault just cause grounds

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance (Rent Board Guide to Coverage)
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered: most units in multifamily properties built before 1980; single-family homes with current tenancies that began before 1996; rooming houses (single-family homes with five or more rooms rented individually with separate leases). Not covered: new construction that received a Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980; single-family homes with tenancies beginning on or after January 1, 1996; most condominiums; certain HUD-subsidized units (Section 202, Section 811, and Rental Supplement/Section 8 projects with HUD-insured or HUD-held mortgages).
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplex (duplex owner-occupied on December 31, 1979 and currently with an owner living in one unit); units where the owner shares a kitchen or bath with the tenant; tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018 on properties with an ADU where either unit is owner-occupied; university rental units such as dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives.
rules.interaction: Partially covered units must still register and remain subject to security deposit interest, but are not subject to rent control or just cause for eviction. The guide does not state the rent cap formula.
rules.quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes
rules.requirement: Rent control under the Berkeley ordinance applies to fully covered units, which include most multifamily units built before 1980, single-family homes with tenancies that began before 1996, and rooming houses. Partially covered and exempt units are not subject to rent control.
rules.title: Berkeley rent control coverage by unit type

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any coordinated pricing algorithm, meaning a process that uses nonpublic Competitor Data (less than 90 days old) to recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms for future leases, in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and its competitors, including through a third-party vendor. Covers residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: Excludes aggregated and anonymous published rental data reports that do not recommend rents, fees or occupancy rates; products used to set rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines; and products used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development (as long as Competitor Data is not used as an input when a recommendation is calculated).
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (City Attorney enforcement)
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.requirement: No one may sell, license, or otherwise provide Berkeley landlords with a coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential units in Berkeley.
rules.title: Ban on selling or providing coordinated pricing algorithms

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords and their agents charging screening fees to applicants for residential rental units.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge an application screening fee if they know or should know that no rental unit is available now or within a reasonable period of time.
rules.title: No screening fee when no unit is available

rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant sends a written request and 30 days pass. Seasonal rentals (125 consecutive days or less) are exempt from the deposit-holding provisions.
rules.interaction: The first month's rent may also be collected at lease inception, so total up-front charges may not exceed 2.5 times monthly rent.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent; yearly increase capped at 10% of current deposit
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half months' rent. Any yearly increase in the deposit may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Prepaid rent held as security, including last month's rent, and pet deposits count toward the cap.
rules.title: Security deposit cap of 1.5 months' rent

rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants evicted under § 98.0704(b)(1), (3) or (4) who requested the offer in writing within 30 days of the termination notice and supplied a mailing or email address.
rules.interaction: The landlord may screen the tenant using industry accepted methods and must state the minimum screening criteria in the offer.
rules.key_value: 5-year re-rental window; 30 days to accept
rules.quoted_span: If a residential rental property is offered for rent or lease for residential purposes within five years of the date the tenant was evicted under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4), landlord shall first offer to lease the residential rental property in writing to the tenant displaced from that unit by the no-fault just cause termination if the tenant:
rules.requirement: If the unit is offered for rent again within five years after a no-fault eviction for owner move-in, government order or demolition/remodel, the landlord must first offer it in writing to the displaced tenant. The tenant has 30 days to accept, provided they asked in writing within 30 days of the termination notice and gave contact details.
rules.title: Right to first offer to re-rent after no-fault eviction

rules.coverage_conditions: Any security deposit received by a lessor of residential real property.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.interaction: Failure to deposit funds as required forfeits the landlord's right to retain any part of the deposit (subsec. 6(a)) and exposes the landlord to treble damages (subsec. 7).
rules.key_value: Separate interest-bearing account in a bank located within the commonwealth
rules.quoted_span: Any security deposit received by such lessor shall be held in a separate, interest-bearing account in a bank, located within the commonwealth under such terms as will place such deposit beyond the claim of creditors of the lessor, including a foreclosing mortgagee or trustee in bankruptcy, and as will provide for its transfer to a subsequent owner of said property.
rules.requirement: A landlord must hold the tenant's deposit in a separate interest-bearing account in a Massachusetts bank, beyond the reach of the landlord's creditors, and give the tenant a receipt naming the bank within 30 days. If the landlord fails to comply, the tenant is entitled to immediate return of the deposit.
rules.title: Security deposit must be held in separate interest-bearing bank account

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (as amended by Measure BB, Nov. 2024)
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully or partially covered units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.interaction: FMR is the figure for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.
rules.key_value: Rental debt at least 1 month of Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR
rules.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict for nonpayment only if the tenant owes at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent for a unit of equivalent size in the Oakland-Fremont metro area.
rules.title: No nonpayment eviction for debt under one month's Fair Market Rent

rules.coverage_conditions: Substantial remodel means replacing or substantially modifying structural, electrical, plumbing or mechanical systems requiring a permit, or abating hazardous materials. Cosmetic work does not qualify.
rules.exemptions: Properties exempt under § 98.0703.
rules.interaction: Triggers relocation assistance under § 98.0706(c) and a right to re-rent at the prior rent if the work is not commenced or completed.
rules.key_value: Work requiring vacancy of at least 30 continuous days; permits secured before notice
rules.quoted_span: The landlord seeks to recover possession to demolish or to substantially remodel the residential rental property.
rules.requirement: A landlord may end a tenancy to demolish or substantially remodel only if the work cannot safely be done with the tenant in place and requires vacating for at least 30 continuous days. Required permits must be secured before notice and the notice must include prescribed certified statements.
rules.title: No-fault just cause: demolition or substantial remodel

rules.coverage_conditions: Rental applications where a government rent subsidy is in place.
rules.exemptions: Does not limit an owner's ability to verify employment, request landlord references, or verify identity (subd. (o)(2)).
rules.quoted_span: Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
rules.requirement: Where there is a government rent subsidy, a landlord using credit history must let the applicant offer alternative verifiable evidence of ability to pay the tenant's share of rent. The landlord must allow reasonable time to respond and reasonably consider that evidence instead of credit history.
rules.title: Alternative evidence option when credit history is used for subsidized rentals

rules.coverage_conditions: Landlord is a natural person (including a settlor or beneficiary of a family trust) or an LLC whose members are all natural persons, and owns no more than two residential rental properties that together include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent. Does not apply to security collected or demanded before 2024-07-01.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member (Military and Veterans Code § 400); the one-month cap in (c)(1) then applies.
rules.interaction: Operates as an exception to the one-month cap in (c)(1); subparagraph (B) returns service member tenants to that cap.
rules.key_value: 2 months' rent
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to two months’ rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy if the landlord meets both of the following requirements:
rules.requirement: A qualifying small landlord may not demand or receive security greater than two months' rent, in addition to first month's rent paid before move-in. This does not apply to service member tenants.
rules.title: Two-month deposit cap for small landlords

rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing providers in Berkeley with respect to current and prospective tenants and applicants.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record resides in one unit as primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.interaction: Written notice and opportunity to respond is required before any adverse action based on criminal history.
rules.key_value: Administrative fines of $1,000 to $10,000 per violation; damages of actual damages or three times one month's rent
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.requirement: Berkeley housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decisions such as refusing to rent, terminating a tenancy, or raising deposit or rent. Landlords must give written notice and an opportunity to respond before taking any action based on criminal history.
rules.title: Fair Chance Access to Housing: ban on using criminal history in tenant selection

rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.interaction: The 5-business-day return period applies to tenants displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation.
rules.key_value: 30 days after termination of tenancy
rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant
rules.requirement: A landlord must return the security deposit plus interest, less lawful deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Any deductions must be itemized and sent by registered or certified mail. A tenant may sue for double the amount wrongfully withheld.
rules.title: Return of security deposit within 30 days

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (security deposit interest requirements)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.
rules.key_value: Annual interest on deposit, prorated on move-out
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year. A prorated amount is due if the tenant moves out before year end.
rules.title: Security deposit interest

rules.coverage_conditions: Units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance: rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28. Eviction notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service.
rules.interaction: Properties not covered by the RSO remain subject to the city's separate Just Cause Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: The owner or immediate family member will move into the rental unit
rules.requirement: Landlords of rent-stabilized units may evict only for listed at-fault reasons (such as non-payment, lease violations, nuisance, illegal use, or refusing access) or listed no-fault reasons (such as owner or family move-in, resident manager move-in, demolition, government order, or conversion to affordable housing). No-fault evictions require a declaration filed with LAHD, written notice, and tenant relocation assistance.
rules.title: RSO just cause eviction grounds and relocation assistance

rules.coverage_conditions: Rental dwelling units offered by a housing provider.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded.
rules.key_value: First-degree: 6 years; second/third-degree: 4 years; fourth-degree: 1 year (from conviction or end of prison sentence, before the conditional offer); no limit for listed serious crimes and lifetime sex offender registry crimes
rules.quoted_span: After the issuance of a conditional offer to an applicant, a housing provider may only consider a criminal record in the applicant’s history that:
rules.requirement: After a conditional offer, a landlord may consider only convictions for certain serious crimes (murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, etc.) or recent indictable offenses within set look-back periods.
rules.title: Limited look-back periods for convictions after a conditional offer

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations; covers recipients of federal, state or local public assistance (including medical assistance) and tenants receiving federal, state or local housing subsidies.
rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient, or because of any requirement of such public assistance, rental assistance, or housing subsidy program.
rules.requirement: Anyone furnishing rental accommodations may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy, such as rental assistance or rental supplements, or because of any requirement of such a program.
rules.title: Source-of-income and housing subsidy discrimination barred in rental accommodations

rules.coverage_conditions: All landlord-tenant relationships.
rules.exemptions: Two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home, and residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex or age-restricted housing (as to familial status).
rules.interaction: The guide notes a landlord may still refuse to rent if the applicant lacks sufficient income or has poor credit history.
rules.quoted_span: prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.
rules.requirement: Landlords and rental agents may not discriminate in renting housing on the basis of source of lawful income, among other protected characteristics.
rules.title: Source of lawful income protected under Law Against Discrimination

rules.coverage_conditions: Leases entered into on or after 2023-06-24 require written tenant agreement or an express lease clause. Does not apply if the intended occupant already occupies a unit on the property or a similar unit is vacant.
rules.exemptions: Properties exempt under § 98.0703.
rules.interaction: Triggers relocation assistance under § 98.0706(c) and the right to re-rent under § 98.0706(d). If the occupant does not move in, the unit must be offered back at the same rent and the tenant reimbursed for moving expenses.
rules.key_value: Intended occupant must occupy within 90 days for at least 12 continuous months
rules.quoted_span: The owner seeks to recover possession to occupy the residential rental property for the owner or their spouse, domestic partner, child (by blood or adoption), grandchild (by blood or adoption), parent, or grandparent for a minimum of 12 continuous months as that person’s primary residence.
rules.requirement: An owner may end a tenancy to move in themselves or a close relative for at least 12 continuous months. For leases entered into on or after June 24, 2023, this applies only if the tenant agrees in writing or the lease expressly allows it. The occupant must move in within 90 days and the landlord must act in good faith.
rules.title: No-fault just cause: owner or relative move-in

rules.coverage_conditions: Housing services including garage facilities, parking facilities, driveways, storage spaces, and laundry rooms in units covered by the Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Temporary removal of services such as parking and storage for mandatory soft-story seismic retrofit work, where the landlord has complied with Ordinance Section 37.2(r).
rules.quoted_span: The landlord also needs a "just cause“ reason to take away or remove access to certain
rules.requirement: A landlord needs a just cause reason to take away or remove access to certain housing services such as garage, parking, storage and laundry facilities. Landlords who comply with Section 37.2(r) may temporarily remove services like parking and storage to perform mandatory soft-story seismic retrofit work.
rules.title: Just cause required to remove housing services

rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property leases and tenancies, other than vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.exemptions: Leases, rentals, occupancies or tenancies of 100 days or less for a vacation or recreational purpose (subsec. 9).
rules.interaction: Lessor may not demand rent in advance beyond the current month or a deposit above the allowed amount after the tenancy begins (subsec. 1(d)). Lease terms that conflict with this section are void (subsec. 8).
rules.key_value: Security deposit no more than 1 month's rent
rules.quoted_span: a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2)
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or agent may collect only first month's rent, last month's rent at the same rate, a security deposit of no more than one month's rent, and the cost of a key and lock. The deposit cap applies only if the deposit is held as required and the tenant gets a statement of condition.
rules.title: Security deposit capped at first month's rent

rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties. Deposit-holding rules differ for landlords holding deposits for 10 or fewer units versus 10 or more.
rules.exemptions: Seasonal rentals (125 consecutive days or less); owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.quoted_span: The security deposit money continues to be the property of the person making the deposit and must be held in trust by the person receiving the money.
rules.requirement: Security deposit money stays the tenant's property and must be held in trust, not commingled with the landlord's own funds. Interest or earnings on the deposit belong to the tenant and are paid in cash or credited to rent.
rules.title: Security deposit held in trust and interest owed to tenant

rules.citation: Boston Fair Housing Regulations, Boston Fair Housing Commission (boston.gov)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to renting, buying, selling, or financing housing in the City of Boston. The page does not state unit-count, year-built, or owner-type limits.
rules.interaction: Enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission alongside local, state, and federal fair housing laws.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord tells you they don't accept rental assistance.
rules.requirement: Landlords in Boston may not discriminate against tenants or applicants because they use rental assistance, such as Section 8, social security disability, or veterans vouchers. Refusing to accept rental assistance is an example of prohibited housing discrimination.
rules.title: Rental assistance (source of income) protected from housing discrimination

rules.coverage_conditions: Rental dwelling units offered by a housing provider.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded.
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
rules.requirement: A landlord may not require an applicant to take a drug or alcohol test or ask for consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
rules.title: No drug or alcohol testing or drug treatment records of applicants

rules.coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.quoted_span: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”
rules.requirement: A lease or rental agreement may not describe any security deposit as nonrefundable.
rules.title: No 'nonrefundable' deposits

rules.coverage_conditions: Rental dwelling units offered for rent by a housing provider; applies to all housing providers (landlords, owners, lessors, agents).
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are not 'rental dwelling units'. Landlords may consider meth-production convictions in federally assisted housing and lifetime sex offender registry status.
rules.interaction: Complaints are handled administratively by the Division on Civil Rights, not in court.
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.requirement: A landlord may not ask about an applicant's criminal record, orally or in writing, or put such questions on the application, until after making a conditional offer. Narrow exceptions apply for methamphetamine manufacture convictions in federally assisted housing and lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.title: No criminal record inquiries before a conditional offer

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person selling, licensing or providing an 'algorithmic device' to a landlord for residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Excludes software that publishes reports from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old or from publicly available information and does not recommend rates or occupancy for future leases or renewals; also excludes software used to set rents or income limits under local, state, or federal affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord.
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to a landlord software that uses nonpublic competitor data to recommend rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property in San Diego.
rules.title: Prohibition on selling or providing algorithmic rent-setting devices

rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (section number not stated in document)
rules.interaction: Tenants and landlords may petition the Rent Stabilization Office to review increases above the maximum, and landlords may charge limited pass-through fees under the Ordinance.
rules.key_value: lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI change; 2.87% for 2026-09-01 to 2027-08-31
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.
rules.requirement: A landlord may raise rent only once a year by a limited amount: no more than 3% of current rent or 80% of the CPI change, whichever is less. For September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027 the city lists the maximum allowable increase as 2.87%.
rules.title: Annual maximum rent increase (lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI change)

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to covered tenancies where termination is based on a curable lease violation.
rules.quoted_span: If the violation is not cured within the time period set forth in the notice, a three-day notice to quit without an opportunity to cure may thereafter be served to terminate the tenancy.
rules.requirement: Before issuing a just cause termination notice for a curable lease violation, the owner must give the tenant notice of the violation and an opportunity to cure it. Only if the violation is not cured may a three-day notice to quit without opportunity to cure be served.
rules.title: Opportunity to cure before terminating for curable lease violation

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (as amended by Measure BB, Nov. 2024)
rules.coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance; includes government-owned or -subsidized units now registered as covered.
rules.exemptions: Exempt units under the Rent Ordinance, including shared kitchen or bath units where the landlord lived on the property at the start of the tenancy.
rules.quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”).
rules.requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered units cannot be evicted unless there is just cause.
rules.title: Just cause required for covered units

rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO), City of Los Angeles
rules.coverage_conditions: All RSO and JCO rental units in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.key_value: Rent owed must exceed the Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit's bedroom count
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).
rules.requirement: A landlord may not evict a tenant for falling behind in rent unless the amount owed is higher than the Fair Market Rent for the unit's bedroom size.
rules.title: Eviction for non-payment of rent limited to arrears above Fair Market Rent

rules.citation: Los Angeles Municipal Code ch. XV, art. 1 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance)
rules.coverage_conditions: Units subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance: rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28.
rules.interaction: Modifies the allowable annual rent increase under the RSO.
rules.key_value: No additional utility percentage; no 10% for an additional dependent
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.requirement: Landlords of rent-stabilized units can no longer add an extra percentage to the allowable rent increase for utilities. An extra 10% for an additional dependent is also no longer permitted, though 10% for an additional non-dependent tenant is still allowed.
rules.title: No utility add-on to RSO rent increase

rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the RSO or JCO. The reduced Mom & Pop amount applies only to owner or relative occupancy evictions, where the building has four or fewer units, the landlord has not used the provision in the prior three years, the landlord owns no more than four units and a single-family home on a separate lot in Los Angeles, and any eligible relative owns no residential property in Los Angeles.
rules.exemptions: No relocation assistance is owed for evicting a resident manager to replace with another resident manager, or for hazardous conditions caused by a natural disaster that the landlord did not negligently cause. The landlord may offset accumulated unpaid rent unless the eviction results from a government order to vacate.
rules.interaction: Demolition of Protected Units for new construction with lower-income tenants is governed by the Resident Protections Ordinance and the state Housing Crisis Act (Gov. Code § 66300.6), whichever amount is higher. The RSO or JCO amounts are the minimum.
rules.key_value: Eligible: $11,000 (<3 yrs) / $14,400 (3+ yrs or low income); Qualified: $23,150 / $27,400; Mom & Pop: $10,550 eligible / $21,250 qualified; JCO single-family owned by natural person: one month's rent (effective July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027)
rules.quoted_span: Payment shall be made available within fifteen (15) days of service of the written notice of eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord who evicts for a no-fault reason must pay relocation assistance per unit. The amount depends on whether the tenant is eligible or qualified (62 or older, disabled, or with minor dependent children), length of tenancy and income. Payment must be made available within 15 days of service of the eviction notice.
rules.title: Relocation assistance required for no-fault evictions

rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Ordinance, S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential units in San Francisco; 'algorithmic device' means a device such as a software program that uses algorithms to analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to give a landlord recommendations on what rent to charge for a vacant unit.
rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of such algorithmic devices and allows a tenant or the City Attorney to bring a civil action if they believe an entity is in violation of the law.
rules.requirement: No one may sell or use an algorithmic device, such as software that analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents for vacant units, to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. A tenant or the City Attorney may bring a civil action over a violation.
rules.title: Prohibition on sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords and their agents who collect an application screening fee from an applicant.
