rules.key_value: Credit report copy within 7 days of receipt
rules.quoted_span:
If the landlord or their agent does
not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, the landlord or their agent shall return any amount of the screening fee that is not used for the purposes authorized by this section to the applicant.
rules.requirement: A landlord must give the applicant an itemized receipt for the fee, return any portion of the fee not used for a reference check or credit report, and give the applicant a copy of the credit report within seven days of receiving it.
rules.title: Receipt, return of unused fee, and credit report copy

rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Board, Current Rates: Allowable Rent Increase (March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027)
rules.interaction: Replaces the prior 1.4% allowable increase that applied March 1, 2025 – February 28, 2026. The page does not state which units are covered.
rules.quoted_span: 1.6% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
rules.requirement: For the period March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027, the Rent Board's allowable annual rent increase is 1.6%.
rules.title: Allowable annual rent increase, March 2026 – February 2027

rules.coverage_conditions: Rentals where a government rent subsidy is in place.
rules.exemptions: Does not limit an owner's ability to request information to verify employment, request landlord references, or verify identity (subd. (o)(2)).
rules.key_value: Income standard based on tenant's share of rent
rules.quoted_span: Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
rules.requirement: When a government rent subsidy applies, a landlord must base any income or financial eligibility standard on the portion of rent the tenant will actually pay.
rules.title: Income standard must reflect tenant's portion of subsidized rent

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (as amended by Measure BB, Nov. 2024)
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully or partially covered units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: The alleged violation must cause substantial, actual damage to the landlord.
rules.requirement: To evict for violating a lease term, the term must be a mutually agreed material term, the violation must cause substantial actual damage to the landlord, and the tenant's behavior must be unreasonable. The notice to stop the violation must specify the term, violation and harm in enough detail for a reasonable person to understand.
rules.title: Lease-violation evictions require material term, actual harm and unreasonable behavior

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (as amended by Measure BB, Nov. 2024)
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of units covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance's rent ceiling.
rules.quoted_span: Landlords can only file a petition for rent increases for completed capital improvements (they can no longer petition to have rent increases preliminarily authorized for planned capital improvements).
rules.requirement: Landlords may only petition for rent increases for completed capital improvements, not planned ones.
rules.title: Capital improvement rent increase petitions limited to completed improvements

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (as amended by Measure BB, Nov. 2024)
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered unit types: most units in multifamily properties built before 1980; single-family homes with current tenancies that began prior to 1996; single-family homes with five or more rooms rented individually with separate leases. Partially covered: new construction units (certificate of occupancy issued after 1980), most single-family homes, most condominiums. Subsidy types such as Section 8 vouchers, Shelter Plus Care, VASH, LIHTC, HOME apply.
rules.exemptions: Section 202 and Section 811 units, and units in projects with HUD-insured or HUD-held mortgages (Rent Supplement, Section 8 Loan Management Set Aside, Project-based Section 8), are only partially covered because Federal law, State law or regulation prohibits rent control.
rules.key_value: Rent increases limited by the Annual General Adjustment
rules.quoted_span: Units that are fully covered will have a rent ceiling, meaning rent increases will be limited by the
rules.requirement: Landlords of government-owned or -subsidized units must register them as fully or partially covered. Fully covered units have a rent ceiling, so increases are limited by the Annual General Adjustment.
rules.title: Government-owned or -subsidized units subject to rent ceiling

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (as amended by Measure BB, Nov. 2024)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants in fully covered units with tenancies starting on or after 2024-02-06.
rules.interaction: A landlord already charging utilities separately may petition the Rent Board to add average utility cost to the rent ceiling.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies starting on or after February 6, 2024, a landlord may charge a tenant in a fully covered unit for utilities only if either: the cost of the  utilities are part of the base rent, or the utility service is separately-metered and the lease requires the tenant to place the utility in the tenant’s name.
rules.requirement: For tenancies starting on or after February 6, 2024, a landlord may charge a tenant in a fully covered unit for utilities only if utility costs are part of the base rent, or the utility is separately metered and the lease requires the tenant to put the account in their name.
rules.title: Utility charges must be in base rent or separately metered

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property subject to Civ. Code § 1947.12 where the same tenant remains in occupancy over a 12-month period. The same exemptions as for the rent cap apply, including housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes).
rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as § 1947.12(d).
rules.interaction: Operates together with the percentage cap in § 1947.12(a)(1); it does not raise that cap.
rules.key_value: max 2 increments per 12 months
rules.quoted_span: If the same tenant remains in occupancy of a unit of residential real property over any 12-month period, the gross rental rate for the unit of residential real property shall not be increased in more than two increments over that 12-month period, subject to the other restrictions of this subdivision governing gross rental rate increase.
rules.requirement: When the same tenant stays in a unit, the landlord may raise the rent no more than twice in any 12-month period. Both increases together must still stay within the annual cap.
rules.title: Maximum two rent increases in 12 months for same tenant

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords (owners of residential rental property) and their agents charging applicants, including guarantors and cosigners, for residential rental units.
rules.interaction: Applies notwithstanding Section 1950.5; the fee is not considered security under Section 1950.5. Does not preempt rules on deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.key_value: Lesser of actual costs or $30 per applicant (CPI-adjustable annually from Jan 1, 1998)
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an applicant a screening fee no greater than actual out-of-pocket costs of gathering information on the applicant, and never more than $30 per applicant, subject to annual CPI adjustment.
rules.title: Application screening fee cap

rules.coverage_conditions: Residential security deposits held for one year or longer from the start of the tenancy.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.interaction: The tenant may deduct unpaid interest from the next rent payment if not paid or noticed within 30 days after the year ends.
rules.key_value: 5% per year (or lesser bank interest actually received)
rules.quoted_span: A lessor of residential real property who holds a security deposit pursuant to this section for a period of one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of the tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year, or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held payable to the tenant at the end of each year of the tenancy.
rules.requirement: A landlord holding a deposit for a year or longer must pay the tenant interest each year at 5% per year, or the lesser amount actually received from the bank. If the tenancy ends before the anniversary, accrued interest is due within 30 days.
rules.title: Annual interest on security deposits

rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), as described in CRD Housing FAQ (calcivilrights.ca.gov/housing)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants and applicants with disabilities who need a service animal or emotional support animal; housing providers covered by FEHA.
rules.interaction: Operates as a reasonable-accommodation requirement under FEHA; AB 468 does not change these housing rules.
rules.key_value: No pet deposit or pet rent for service/ESA animals
rules.quoted_span: Service animals and emotional-support animals are not subject to breed, size, or weight restrictions ordinarily applied to pets, and tenants cannot be charged pet deposits or pet rent for them.
rules.requirement: Landlords with no-pets rules must make exceptions as a reasonable accommodation for service animals and emotional support animals. Tenants cannot be charged pet deposits or pet rent for them.
rules.title: No pet deposits or pet rent for service or emotional support animals

rules.coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord shall not assert a claim against the tenant or the security for damages to the premises or any defective conditions that preexisted the tenancy, for ordinary wear and tear or the effects thereof, whether the wear and tear preexisted the tenancy or occurred during the tenancy, or for the cumulative effects of ordinary wear and tear occurring during any one or more tenancies.
rules.requirement: A landlord may not claim against the tenant or the deposit for pre-existing damage, ordinary wear and tear, or the cumulative effects of ordinary wear and tear. Deductions are limited to amounts reasonably necessary for unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear, cleaning to move-in condition, and certain property restoration.
rules.title: No deductions for ordinary wear and tear or pre-existing damage

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance (Rent Board Guide to Coverage)
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered: most units in multifamily properties built before 1980; single-family homes with current tenancies that began before 1996; rooming houses with five or more rooms rented individually with separate leases. Not covered: new construction with Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980; single-family homes with tenancies beginning on or after January 1, 1996; most condominiums; certain HUD-subsidized units.
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplex (owner-occupied December 31, 1979 and currently with an owner in one unit); units where the owner shares a kitchen or bath with the tenant; tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018 on properties with an ADU where either unit is owner-occupied; university rental units; nonprofit cooperatives.
rules.interaction: Units listed as Partially Covered are registered and subject to security deposit interest but not to just cause. The guide does not list the permitted grounds for eviction.
rules.quoted_span: Single family homes with current tenancies that began before 1996** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes
rules.requirement: Landlords of fully covered units, including most multifamily units built before 1980, must have just cause to evict. Partially covered and exempt units are not subject to the just cause requirement.
rules.title: Berkeley just cause for eviction coverage by unit type

rules.citation: California state law (as described by Berkeley Rent Board)
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords under California law. The photograph requirement applies after the landlord regains possession and before any repairs or cleaning for which a deduction will be made.
rules.key_value: 21 days
rules.quoted_span: If deductions were made, the landlord must give the tenant a written statement itemizing the amount of and and purpose for any security deposit deductions, accompanied by copies of documents showing charges incurred and deducted by the landlord to repair or clean the premises, including a copy of any bill, invoice, or receipt for materials or supplies deductions.
rules.requirement: The landlord must return the deposit, or any remaining portion, within 21 days after the tenant vacates. If deductions are made, the landlord must provide an itemized written statement with supporting documents. Since January 1, 2025 the landlord must also provide proof that repairs were completed. Since April 1, 2025 the landlord must provide after-possession photographs and a written explanation of repair or cleaning costs.
rules.title: Return of deposit and itemized statement

rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or Just Cause Ordinance (JCO). Resident manager occupancy evictions are allowed only if required by law, an affordable housing covenant or a regulatory agreement.
rules.interaction: RSO units withdrawn from rental use are Ellis Act evictions and must follow LAMC 151.22-151.28. Owner or relative occupancy evictions must meet LAMC 151.30.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord evicts for the occupancy of her/himself, spouse, grandchildren, children, parents or grandparents, or a resident manager
rules.requirement: A landlord of a unit covered by the RSO or JCO may end a tenancy for a no-fault reason only on the listed grounds. These include occupancy by the owner, a relative or a resident manager, demolition, conversion or removal from rental use, a government order to vacate, and certain HUD, residential hotel and affordable housing conversions.
rules.title: Permitted no-fault grounds for eviction under RSO and JCO

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any 'person' (as defined in Bus. & Prof. Code § 16702), excluding the end consumer. A 'common pricing algorithm' is any methodology, including a computer, software, or other technology, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or otherwise influence a price or commercial term. Not specific to residential rental housing.
rules.exemptions: End consumers of a product or service are not 'persons' under the section.
rules.interaction: Does not impair or limit the applicability of other antitrust laws (Cartwright Act, subsection (c)). Complaint pleading standard is set by § 16756.1.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce. This is a general pricing rule and is not limited to housing, but it reaches rent-setting software.
rules.title: Unlawful use or distribution of a common pricing algorithm as part of an antitrust conspiracy

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (as amended by Measure BB, Nov. 2024)
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully or partially covered units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease when a fixed-term lease expires.
rules.title: No eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar lease

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person operating algorithmic revenue management software or an algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function for any rental property owner, including an owner doing so for its own benefit. Excludes spreadsheets operating without AI and requiring human analysis, and databases that only use an algorithm to query unprocessed data.
rules.exemptions: Government entities setting or limiting rents through affordability controls; research/statistical/testing use; free public rent estimates; equal-terms brokerage listing databases that do not set or recommend prices.
rules.interaction: Additional to the New Jersey Antitrust Act, and does not authorize conduct already unlawful under it; municipalities may not enact conflicting ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: a coordinator to facilitate a tacit or express agreement among rental property owners that restricts competition with respect to residential dwelling units, including by performing a coordinating function;
rules.requirement: A coordinator may not facilitate a tacit or express agreement among landlords that restricts competition, including by performing a coordinating function such as pooling nonpublic landlord data in an algorithm to set or recommend rents, lease terms or occupancy levels. Any person performing a coordinating function, and any party engaging in or facilitating parallel pricing coordination, also violates the Act.
rules.title: Coordinators barred from facilitating rent-restricting agreements or performing a coordinating function

rules.citation: N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq. (New Jersey Law Against Discrimination)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to the sale or rental of all property, including open land, for business or residential purposes.
rules.exemptions: Rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit as a residence; rental of a room or rooms by the owner or occupant of an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; preference for persons of the same religion by a religious organization.
rules.quoted_span: This means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful income.
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or the source of lawful rent payment a tenant uses. For example, a landlord cannot refuse to rent to someone solely because they pay with a Section 8 HUD voucher.
rules.title: Source of lawful income / rent payment discrimination prohibited

rules.coverage_conditions: Owners or owner's agents who receive a request to rent residential property in Berkeley and charge a fee for a credit report and application processing.
rules.interaction: Fee cap statement refers to Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b).
rules.quoted_span: the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
rules.requirement: When charging a fee to purchase a credit report and process an application, the owner must provide a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap, either in the application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee.
rules.title: Required disclosure of tenant screening fee rights and fee cap

rules.coverage_conditions: Rental dwelling units offered by a housing provider.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded.
rules.key_value: Preponderance of the evidence standard; applicant request within 30 days; landlord response within 10 days
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider may withdraw a conditional offer based on an applicant's criminal record only if the housing provider determines, by preponderance of the evidence, that the withdrawal is necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest.
rules.requirement: A landlord may withdraw a conditional offer because of a criminal record only if necessary to serve a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest, after an individualized assessment, and must give written reasons and a chance to appeal. The applicant may request copies of information relied on within 30 days, provided free within 10 days.
rules.title: Conditions for withdrawing a conditional offer based on criminal record

rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Board, Annual Rent Increase for 3/1/26 - 2/28/27 Announced (Jan. 14, 2026)
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent-controlled units in San Francisco; allowable increase applies for the period March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027.
rules.interaction: Supersedes the prior-year allowable increase of 1.4% (March 1, 2025 through February 28, 2026).
rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent.
rules.title: San Francisco annual allowable rent increase, March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies-at-will and written leases where a security deposit was taken.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.interaction: No deduction for damage listed in the move-in statement of condition. Missing the deadline or an invalid itemization forfeits the right to retain any deposit (subsec. 6) and triggers treble damages plus 5% interest and attorney's fees (subsec. 7).
rules.key_value: 30 days to return deposit
rules.quoted_span: The lessor shall, within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement, return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof
rules.requirement: The landlord must return the deposit, or the balance, within 30 days after the tenancy ends. The landlord may deduct only unpaid rent or water charges, certain unpaid tax increases, and reasonable repair costs for tenant-caused damage (excluding normal wear and tear), supported by a sworn itemized list.
rules.title: Return of security deposit within 30 days; limited deductions

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley using a coordinated pricing algorithm (one using nonpublic Competitor Data less than 90 days old, in coordination with competitors, including via a third-party vendor).
rules.exemptions: Excludes aggregated and anonymous published rental data reports that do not recommend rents, fees or occupancy rates; products used to set rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines; and products used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development (as long as Competitor Data is not used as an input when a recommendation is calculated).
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; per-month, per-unit violations; prevailing tenant gets attorney's fees
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.requirement: A Berkeley landlord may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential units. Each month of violation and each unit for which the algorithm was used is a separate violation, and tenants may sue for damages, injunctive relief and penalties.
rules.title: Ban on landlord use of coordinated pricing algorithms

rules.coverage_conditions: All tenants in a building converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, including those without protected tenancy status.
rules.quoted_span: rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the conversion
rules.requirement: When a building is converted to a condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, rents may not be raised to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion. Rents may still rise to cover new services or amenities.
rules.title: No rent increase to recover condominium/cooperative conversion costs

rules.coverage_conditions: Intended occupant must be the owner or the owner's spouse, domestic partner, child, grandchild, parent, or grandparent. Not available if the intended occupant occupies a rental unit on the property or a similar unit is already vacant. For leases entered into on or after July 1, 2020 (July 1, 2022 for mobilehomes), requires written tenant agreement or a lease provision allowing owner-move-in termination.
rules.key_value: Move in within 90 days; occupy for at least 12 consecutive months
rules.quoted_span: Clause (i) applies only if the intended occupant moves into the rental unit within 90 days after the tenant vacates and occupies the rental unit as a primary residence for at least 12 consecutive months.
rules.requirement: An owner may terminate for owner or family move-in only if the intended occupant moves in within 90 days after the tenant vacates and lives there as a primary residence for at least 12 consecutive months. If not, the owner must offer the unit back to the tenant at the same rent and terms and reimburse reasonable excess moving expenses.
rules.title: Owner move-in no-fault termination conditions

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies only if and when the executive office of housing and livable communities promulgates implementing regulations; the document does not state that such regulations exist.
rules.interaction: The fee must be optional for tenant and landlord, offered to every approved applicant regardless of income, credit score and similar factors, and may be partly or wholly non-refundable if disclosed and agreed in writing.
rules.key_value: Fee plus any deposit not to exceed 1 month's rent
rules.quoted_span: the executive office of housing and livable communities may promulgate regulations to authorize a lessor and a tenant or prospective tenant to agree to the payment of a fee in lieu of payment of a security deposit
rules.requirement: The state housing office may issue regulations letting a landlord and tenant agree to an optional fee instead of a security deposit. The fee, together with any deposit, may not exceed one month's rent in total, and the tenant may choose to pay a full deposit instead.
rules.title: Authorization for optional fee in lieu of security deposit (by regulation)

rules.citation: California state law (as described by Berkeley Rent Board)
rules.coverage_conditions: Cleaning deductions apply to tenancies beginning after January 1, 2003.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord may deduct only the amount that is reasonably necessary to:
rules.requirement: A landlord may deduct from the deposit only what is reasonably necessary to cover unpaid rent, repair damage beyond normal wear and tear, and clean the unit to its move-in condition. If the lease allows, the landlord may also deduct for restoring or replacing personal property or furniture, excluding ordinary wear and tear. A landlord cannot charge for professional cleaning unless it is reasonably necessary to restore the unit's move-in condition.
rules.title: Permitted security deposit deductions

rules.coverage_conditions: Applicants for residential rental units in Berkeley.
rules.interaction: Reflects California Civil Code Section 1950.6.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot charge a screening fee when no rental unit is actually available. The landlord must refund the fee to applicants not selected, or instead review applications in the order received and not charge applicants who are not considered.
rules.title: No screening fee if no unit available; refund or first-come policy

rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of any housing accommodation; 'source of income' means lawful, verifiable income paid to a tenant, a tenant's representative, or a landlord on the tenant's behalf, including public assistance and housing subsidies.
rules.exemptions: Asking about the level or source of income is not discrimination under subdivision (p)(2).
rules.quoted_span: For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
rules.requirement: A housing owner may not discriminate against or harass anyone because of their source of income, which includes government subsidies such as Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers. Landlords may still ask about the level or source of income.
rules.title: Source-of-income discrimination prohibited in housing

rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties, including single-family homes, mobile homes, apartment buildings and rooming and boarding houses.
rules.exemptions: Hotel/motel guests and seasonal tenants; owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are covered only by a narrower list of grounds.
rules.quoted_span: An eviction is an actual removal of a tenant from the premises. A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant
rules.requirement: A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant, and the landlord must prove the grounds in court. Each cause except nonpayment of rent must be described in detail in a written notice to the tenant.
rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: good cause required to evict

rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental units in buildings constructed on or before 1995-02-01, and mobile home spaces offered for rent on or before 1990-01-01. The source gives construction dates, not certificate-of-occupancy dates.
rules.exemptions: Residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995, and mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990. Owners may petition for relief from the cap by showing a higher increase is needed for a fair and reasonable return.
rules.interaction: The City publishes the allowable increase by June 30 each year, effective September 1. The first figure was due by November 19, 2021.
rules.key_value: lower of 3% per year or 80% of CPI change (no increase if CPI negative)
rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period.
rules.requirement: Annual residential rent increases are capped at the lower of 3% or 80% of the CPI change over the most recent 12 months. If CPI is negative, no increase is allowed.
rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance annual rent cap

rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), as described in CRD Housing FAQ (calcivilrights.ca.gov/housing)
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers covered by FEHA, including tenant screening companies acting for them.
rules.quoted_span: providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system.
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not consider arrests that did not lead to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile justice records, and may not impose blanket bans on people with a criminal history. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to the applicant's ability to be a good tenant and to the safety of others and the property.
rules.title: Limits on use of criminal history in tenant screening

rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the RSO or JCO. For demolition for new construction, Bulletin B states the copy of the notice must be filed within 3 business days.
rules.interaction: Bulletin B applies a Notice of Intent to Withdraw Units (Ellis Act) for RSO units and a Declaration of Intent to Evict for JCO units in demolition cases.
rules.key_value: Copy of notice filed with LAHD within 3 days of service
rules.quoted_span: Notices to terminate tenancy can only be served on the tenant after the landlord files the Declaration with LAHD, and a copy of the notice must be filed with LAHD no later than 3 days after it is served.
rules.requirement: For a no-fault eviction, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving a termination notice. A copy of the notice must then be filed with LAHD within 3 days of service. Failing to file the Declaration makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO.
rules.title: Declaration of Intent to Evict must be filed before no-fault termination notice

rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property for dwelling purposes offered for lease or sublease by a landlord or agent in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: A dwelling unit in a one-family or two-family dwelling that is offered for rent; a New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensee, unless the licensee is the landlord of the property.
rules.key_value: $50 maximum, adjusted annually for CPI increases (NY-Northern NJ-Long Island CPI-U); penalties up to $500 first offense, $750 second, $1,000 each subsequent offense
rules.quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge more than $50 for an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property. Violators face civil penalties and the excess fee must be refunded to the applicant out of the collected penalty. The cap is adjusted each January 1 by the Consumer Price Index change, but only if that change is greater than zero.
rules.title: Residential rental application fee capped at $50

rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO), City of Los Angeles
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO). Applies once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first. The page says the JCO can apply to buildings newer than October 1, 1978, and to a property with only one single-family dwelling.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit facilities for the homeless or short-term substance abuse treatment centers, and some HACLA or government-owned properties.
rules.interaction: Units already subject to the RSO are not covered by the JCO. The JCO does not regulate rent increases.
rules.key_value: At-fault and no-fault just cause reasons; relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a covered tenancy without just cause. Landlords must pay relocation assistance when the eviction is for a no-fault reason.
rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)

rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (adopted 2021)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental tenancies in Santa Ana, other than the excluded property types.
rules.exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; and other shared living quarters.
rules.key_value: just cause required after 30 days
rules.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.
rules.requirement: After a tenancy has lasted 30 days, an owner may not terminate it without just cause, which must be stated in a written notice. For at-fault causes the owner must first give notice of the violation and time to cure it.
rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords and their agents collecting screening fees from applicants for residential rental units.
rules.exemptions: No refund required for an applicant whose application is denied after consideration for failing the landlord's established screening criteria under the first-come process option.
rules.key_value: Full refund within 7 days of selection or 30 days of application, whichever first (alternative option)
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee only if the landlord or their agent, at the time the application screening fee is collected, offers any of the following:
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee only if they offer either a first-come, first-qualified screening process (with written criteria and no fee until the application is actually considered) or a full refund of the fee to any applicant not selected, within 7 days of selecting a tenant or 30 days of application, whichever is first.
rules.title: Conditions for charging a screening fee: first-come process or full refund

rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties.
rules.exemptions: Seasonal rentals (125 consecutive days or less); owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.key_value: Annual interest payment to tenant
rules.quoted_span: The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant
rules.requirement: Interest earned on the security deposit belongs to the tenant. It must be paid in cash or credited toward rent on the lease renewal or anniversary date, or on January 31 if the tenant was given written notice.
rules.title: Interest on deposit belongs to tenant

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (as amended by Measure BB, Nov. 2024)
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered rental units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance, including government-owned or -subsidized units registered as fully covered.
rules.exemptions: Partially covered and exempt units are not subject to the rent ceiling.
rules.interaction: Cap does not prevent a landlord with banked (unused) AGAs from raising rent above 5% to reach the rent ceiling.
rules.key_value: CPI-based formula, maximum 5%
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%.
rules.requirement: The Rent Board's yearly Annual General Adjustment (the allowed annual rent increase for fully covered units) cannot exceed 5%, even if the CPI formula produces a higher figure. Landlords with banked AGAs may still raise rent above 5% to reach the rent ceiling.
rules.title: Annual General Adjustment capped at 5%

rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of residential rental property in Berkeley (or their agents) charging existing tenants.
rules.interaction: Chapter 13.78 applies regardless of contrary lease language; violating lease provisions are unenforceable (BMC 13.78.018).
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.requirement: Owners cannot charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees tied to a roommate leaving, or to request adding or replacing a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.title: Prohibition of non-refundable fees for existing tenancies

rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Board, Current Rates: Security Deposit Interest (March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027)
rules.interaction: Replaces the prior 5.0% rate that applied March 1, 2025 – February 28, 2026.
rules.quoted_span: 4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
rules.requirement: For the period March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027, the Rent Board sets the interest rate on security deposits at 4.2%.
rules.title: Security deposit interest rate, March 2026 – February 2027
